title: Fix result ordering in retrieved context, if BENCH-1 confirms it's a factor
summary: Sort search() results chronologically (or add an explicit ordering option) before joining into retrieved_context, so temporal/update questions aren't fed evidence in a scrambled order the flat baseline never sees.
description:
Conditional on BENCH-1 confirming ordering is a real contributor to the temporal_reasoning/knowledge_update gap. `store.working.search()` ranks by vector distance to the query; `benchmarks/retrieval_quality/run.py`'s with-SDK path joins `results` in that rank order (`"\n".join(r.content for r in results)`), while `run_baseline()` joins turns in original session/chronological order. If BENCH-1's evidence shows this reordering flips judge verdicts, fix it at the layer BENCH-1's evidence points to:

- **If a harness-only concern**: sort `results` by `created_at` before building `retrieved_context` in `run_retrieval_quality()` — a small, local change, no SDK API change, no migration.
- **If real callers of `search()` would hit the same problem** (not just this synthetic benchmark): consider whether `MemoryStore`/`BaseRepository.search()` should support an explicit ordering option (e.g. `order_by="relevance"` default vs `"chronological"`) — this is the larger, SDK-level version of the fix and should only be pursued if BENCH-1's evidence shows this is a general retrieval-quality problem, not a benchmark-harness artifact. Justify the choice in DECISIONS.md either way.

Before starting: read DECISIONS.md in full, including BENCH-1's findings entry. Before finishing: re-run `--suite retrieval --baseline` at the same seed=42/n=10-per-category config as Run B, record the new category deltas in BENCHMARKS.md as a new dated run (don't overwrite Run B — append), append a dated DECISIONS.md entry, set BENCH-2's status to "Done" in BOARD.html with a comment summarizing the fix and the before/after delta, then `git add -A && git commit -m "bench-2: fix search() result ordering in retrieval-quality suite"`. If BENCH-1 refutes the ordering hypothesis, close this story as "Done" with a comment explaining why no change was needed, rather than leaving it stuck In Progress.

comments.text:
Closed without code change. BENCH-1 refuted the ordering hypothesis.

BENCH-1's --debug instrumentation showed that every failing question in every diagnostic run returned results (0 retrieved) from store.working.search() — zero results, not a scrambled order. There is no reordering artifact to fix because there is nothing to reorder.

Root cause is the ORC-2 chunk-path routing bug (search() auto-detect routes all searches through _search_via_chunks() which queries memory_chunks; benchmark turns are short, below chunk_threshold=2000, so memory_chunks is empty and search() returns []). The ordering difference between distance-rank and session order is a latent confound that will be worth revisiting once the ORC-2 fix lands and search() actually returns results, but it is not a measurable contributor to the current gap.

No SDK API change, no harness change, no BENCHMARKS.md re-run needed — there is nothing to measure before/after because the code is unchanged. See DECISIONS.md BENCH-2 entry.
